text:
emily: Thanks everyone — quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: runtime roadmap. A few short clarifying q's so we can sync with infra and PMs. 1) Kernel prioritization: are the sparse-attention kernels still on the same sprint as the quantization improvements? 2) KV cache eviction default — LRU or TTL-first? 3) Auto-batching thresholds: what's the recommended batch_ms vs tail-latency SLO tradeoff for Hosted vs Dedicated? @sam @raj can you confirm?
sam: Short answers — sparse kernels are gated but still in the sprint, quant work is on a slightly different track (kickoff next week). KV eviction is LRU by default, TTL only for explicit tenant config. Will add details to the kernel RFC.
raj: Re: batching, we're seeing good cost wins at batch_ms=10 for typical chat workloads but tail latency rises for p95/p99 with long seqs. For Dedicated we can push batch_ms to 20 with prewarm.
kevin: For SRE telemetry, note that p99 is dominated by cold-starts and long-seq requests. Suggest adding a cold-start flag in traces so we can filter.
maria: From PM: we need concrete guidance for customers on "safe" batching settings per workload class (chat vs embed vs rerank). I'll draft a table once we have numbers.
dina: Action item: can infra share a recommended defaults snippet we can put in docs? Also need note on canary plan if kernel regresses.
lisa: I'll pair with Sam to pull perf numbers (seq length buckets + token cost) and provide a small CSV for the PM table. ETA EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
sam: Adding a config example for docs — feel free to reuse: 
```
runtime_defaults:
  batching:
    batch_ms: 10
    max_batch_tokens: 4096
  kv_cache:
    policy: LRU
    ttl_seconds: 0  # 0 => disabled unless tenant sets
  tail_latency_slo_ms: 150
```
raj: Note on kernel prioritization: sparse-attn offers good mem/compute tradeoffs but only benefits models with long contexts > 4k. We're prioritizing quant kernels for 2–4k models first per customer telemetry.
emily: Helpful — can we get a short blurb for the all-hands notes summarizing: sparse-attn on sprint X, quant on sprint Y, LRU default, batch_ms recommended defaults, owners (Sam/Raj/Lisa)?
sam: Yep — I'll post a 3-line summary in this thread by EOD.
dina: Also, production rollback hook is in the release playbook but not obvious. @kevin can you link the playbook?
kevin: linked playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/kernel-release — rollback steps + canary gating are there. I also added a checklist item to run the new kernel perf test suite in CI.
maria: Small ask: can we include cost delta per setting (e.g., batch_ms 10 -> 20 = ~12% token cost reduction for chat baseline)? Even rough numbers help sales/customer convos.
lisa: I'll include a cost column in the CSV.
deploy-bot: deploy-notify: canary rollout for kernel-v11 scheduled for 2026-03-29 02:00 UTC (window: 2h).
emily: Perfect — thanks everyone. I'll compile notes and owners and post summary in #all-hands-notes. If anyone wants to be removed from follow-ups, say so here.
sam: +1, will follow up on the kernel RFC and paste link.
raj: I'll prep infra sizing guidance for Dedicated (prewarm + batch_ms tradeoffs).
kevin: I'll confirm CI perf tests are green before canary.
dina: Filing a doc task for PM to track (TICKET-5123).
maria: Thanks — this unblocks the customer-facing guidance.
lisa: Done — will share CSV draft tomorrow morning. :rocket:
